Let \(A_i\) be the \(105\times105\) adjacency matrix joining two perfect matchings at distance \(i\). For two matchings, their union decomposes into alternating cycles; if the corresponding partition of \(4\) has \(r\) parts, then

\[
d(M,N)=4-r.
\]

Thus the distance shells have sizes

\[
1,\ 12,\ 44,\ 48
\]

for distances \(0,1,2,3\), and

\[
D_p=A_1+2^pA_2+3^pA_3.
\]

The action of \(S_8\) on perfect matchings is multiplicity-free, with irreducible dimensions

\[
1,\ 20,\ 14,\ 56,\ 14.
\]

On the nonconstant components, the eigenvalues of \(D_p\) are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{dimension} & \lambda(p)\\
\hline
20 & 5+2\cdot 2^p-8\cdot 3^p\\
14 & -6+11\cdot 2^p-6\cdot 3^p\\
56 & -1-4\cdot 2^p+4\cdot 3^p\\
14 & 2-2^p-2\cdot 3^p
\end{array}
\]

The metric has \(p\)-negative type exactly when all these nonconstant eigenvalues are \(\le 0\). The only first crossing comes from the \(56\)-dimensional component:

\[
-1-4\cdot 2^p+4\cdot 3^p=0,
\]

i.e.

\[
4(3^p-2^p)=1.
\]

This equation has a unique positive root because \(3^p-2^p\) is strictly increasing for \(p>0\). Numerically,

\[
\wp \approx 0.4219679707924078.
\]

At this value, only the \(56\)-dimensional eigenspace has eigenvalue \(0\), so

\[
\dim E=56.
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{(\wp,\dim E)=\left(\text{the unique positive root of }4(3^p-2^p)=1,\ 56\right)}.
\]
